content.text:
**[PR #197](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/197) is up; MM-297 is In Review.** Summary of this round:

**The bug**: the consent page rendered its `granted_scope` checkboxes *before* opening the `<form>` element. Browsers only submit controls inside the form, so the checkboxes were never posted, and the consent filter reduced **every OAuth grant Custos ever issued through its real consent page to bare `atproto`** — silently, with the UI showing checked boxes the whole time. It stayed invisible because the wallet's only other OAuth flow requests exactly `atproto` anyway; the orchestrator's `transition:generic` request was the first that needed more.

**The diagnosis trail became regression tests**: while isolating the failure I proved each server stage individually — PAR stores the scope, a consent POST that *does* carry the checkbox stores the full scope, the DPoP token exchange preserves it, and `getServiceAuth` honors `transition:generic`. All three new tests are in the PR, including a wallet-shaped end-to-end that is the orchestrator's exact first source call (the existing outbound-migration integration test authenticates with a legacy full-session token, which is why CI never caught either MM-295 or this). Plus a structural template test that fails on the old markup. Full suite 1743+1 green, clippy/fmt clean.

**One important note for the retest**: after this merges and staging deploys, don't just tap retry — the source client in memory holds a token with `atproto` baked in, and even a refresh preserves that stored scope. **Restart the migration flow from the start screen** so it runs a fresh OAuth login through the fixed consent page. When you land on that page, you should see "transition:generic" as a checked box — leave it checked.

Same watcher pattern as last time once you merge: I'll track CI → staging deploy and tell you when it's safe to go. Two rehearsal runs, two Urgent bugs that would otherwise have shipped to your phone run — leg (r) is earning its keep.

input.title: putPreferences/getPreferences reject deactivated accounts — blocks migration preference import before activateAccount
input.description:
## Found by

MM-241 leg (r) rehearsal, third blocker. After MM-295 + MM-297, the orchestrator cleared getServiceAuth, created the deactivated destination account on production, transferred the repo and drained blobs — then died at the preferences step:

```
putPreferences → 401 {"error":{"code":"INVALID_TOKEN","message":"account not found"}}
```

## Root cause

`routes/put_preferences.rs` (and `get_preferences.rs`) gate on `db::accounts::account_is_active`, which requires `deactivated_at`/`suspended_at`/`taken_down_at` all NULL. A migrating **destination** account is deactivated *by design* until `activateAccount` — the standard ATProto migration sequence (createAccount-deactivated → importRepo → uploadBlob → putPreferences → checkAccountStatus → activateAccount) requires preference import pre-activation, and the reference PDS permits it (its preferences routes check takedown, not deactivation). `importRepo`, `uploadBlob`, `checkAccountStatus`, `getRecommendedDidCredentials`, and `getServiceAuth` all already tolerate/expect the deactivated state; the two preferences routes are the odd ones out.

## Fix

Replace the `account_is_active` gate in both preferences routes with an exists + not-takendown/not-suspended check (deactivated allowed) — reference parity: the reference blocks moderation states, not self-service deactivation. Tests: putPreferences and getPreferences succeed on a deactivated account; still 401/rejected for takendown and for a deleted account.

## Deployment need

Same train as MM-295/297: staging for legs (r)/(b)/(c), production before leg (d).

**[PR #198](https://github.com/malpercio-dev/ezpds/pull/198) is up; MM-298 In Review.** Fix: both preferences routes now admit deactivated accounts (via a new unfiltered `account_lifecycle` lookup) while still refusing taken-down/suspended/missing ones — reference parity, since the standard migration sequence imports preferences into the deactivated destination before `activateAccount`. I also audited every other route the orchestrator still needs (`checkAccountStatus`, `getRecommendedDidCredentials`, `activateAccount`) — no more lifecycle gates on the path, so this should be the last blocker of this class. `account_is_active` is gone entirely (the preferences routes were its only callers); its test coverage moved to the new helper. 1745+1 tests, clippy, fmt all green.

**One deployment wrinkle this time, and it matters:** this failure came from the **destination** — production (obsign.org), which is still running v0.4.3 with *none* of tonight's fixes. Staging auto-deploys on merge, but that's not enough anymore:

- Leg (r)'s destination is production → needs MM-298 there.
- And when the flow later reaches production as a *source* (leg d, or any production-side OAuth), it needs MM-295 + MM-297 there too.

So after you merge #198, the clean move is a patch release carrying the whole train: `just set-version 0.4.4` PR → merge → `just release` → `just deploy-production v0.4.4`. That puts both servers on identical code and clears every deploy dependency for legs (r) through (d) in one shot.

Also for the retest: the half-migrated throwaway on production (deactivated account, repo + blobs already imported) is fine to leave — the orchestrator's early steps are idempotent, so restarting the flow from the start screen will reuse/re-create cleanly. And since the failure was *after* source auth, the fresh OAuth login you did this run already proved the MM-297 consent fix works — the token carried `transition:generic` all the way through `getServiceAuth`, account creation, repo transfer, and blob drain. Three steps from the finish line.

input.title: Migration-mode createAccount is not resumable — a mid-flight failure strands the migration with a 409
input.description:
## Found by

MM-241 leg (r) rehearsal, fourth blocker: retrying the migration after the MM-298 failure hits

```
createAccount 409 with no dest_client; destination conflict did=did:plc:qguep…
```

The wallet orchestrator's idempotency only holds in memory (it tolerates the 409 if it still holds the session from the first `createAccount`); after an app restart there is nothing to resume with. And the wallet flow deliberately sets **no destination password** (Custos accounts are passwordless-mobile), so the goat-style retry path — log back in with `createSession` — does not exist either. Any mid-flight failure between `createAccount` and `activateAccount` permanently strands the migration. This threatens the real leg (b) on the phone, not just rehearsals.

Compounding landmines on the retry path (all bypassed by the fix below): `ensure_email_and_handle_free` would trip on the half-created account's own email/handle rows, and the reserved-signing-key check fails after the key was promoted at first creation.

## Fix (server-side, no wallet change)

In `create_account_migration` (`routes/create_account_xrpc.rs`), immediately after `verify_service_auth_jwt` succeeds, check `account_lifecycle(did)`:

- `None` → current creation path, unchanged.
- `Some(Deactivated)` → **resume**: issue a fresh session for the existing account and return 200 (stored handle, freshly resolved DID doc). Rationale: the service-auth JWT is the *same credential* that authorized creating the account — aud-bound to this server, lxm-bound to createAccount, signed by the DID's current `#atproto` key — so re-presenting a fresh one proves the same DID control. No invite code is consumed on resume.
- `Some(Active | Suspended | TakenDown)` → 409 as today (a live account is a genuine conflict; moderation states stay closed).

The wallet's existing 409 arm remains for foreign (reference) destinations, which are not resumable without a password.

## Deployment need

Dest-side: production (leg r/b/c destinations = production/staging/production… staging for (b), production for (r)/(c)) — i.e. both, via the next patch release.

- **Tonight's leg (r):** mint a **fresh throwaway** on staging and run the flow with it — a new DID never hits the conflict, and v0.4.4 (already live on both ends) has everything a clean run needs. Preferences was the last pipeline blocker; a fresh run should go the distance.

Fold it into production with the next patch release before leg (c); the stranded `did:plc:qguep…` account then even doubles as a live test — re-running the old migration against it should resume instead of 409.

input.title: Post-migration/recovery DID-doc cache stores the W3C document — home badge degrades to "Unknown" (no rotationKeys)
input.description:
## Found by

MM-241 leg (r) — the migration itself succeeded and verified clean on plc.directory (endpoint → obsign.org, device key at rotationKeys[0]), but the wallet's home card then showed the **"Unknown"** custody badge for the migrated identity.

## Root cause

The wallet caches a **PLC-format** DID document per identity (`{did, alsoKnownAs, rotationKeys, verificationMethods, services}` — what `claim::submit_claim` builds and the create flow synthesizes). `IdentityListHome.isDeviceKeyRoot` reads `didDoc.rotationKeys[0]`; `extractPdsFromPlcDoc` reads the `services` map.

But the post-submit cache refresh in **`migrate::submit_migration_op`** and **`recovery::submit_recovery_override`** fetches `GET {plc.directory}/{did}` — the **W3C DID document** (`@context/id/alsoKnownAs/verificationMethod/service[]`), which carries **no `rotationKeys`** and a different service shape — and stores it via `store_did_doc`, clobbering the good PLC-format cache. Result: `deviceKeyIsRoot === null` → "Unknown" badge (and the card's PDS-host line degrades too).

## Fix

Fetch `GET {plc.directory}/{did}/data` (the PLC data document — exactly the cached shape: `did, alsoKnownAs, rotationKeys, services, verificationMethods`) in both `submit_migration_op` and `submit_recovery_override`. Wallet-only change; simulator-testable; no server deploy.

Note: an identity whose cache was already clobbered (the leg (r) throwaway) stays "Unknown" until the next flow re-stores its doc — acceptable, it's disposable.

input.title: Claim flow caches empty rotationKeys (W3C doc parse) — migrate button hidden for claimed identities; add cache self-heal
input.description:
## Found by

MM-241 leg (b) prep: on the phone, the claimed bsky.social identity shows no "Migrate to another PDS" button (and the "Unknown" custody badge).

## Root cause

Same disease as MM-300, third vector. `+page.svelte` wires `onmigrate` only when `deviceKeyIsRoot === true`, which `IdentityListHome` derives from the cached doc's `rotationKeys[0]`. `claim::submit_claim`'s post-claim re-fetch goes through `discover_pds`, which parses plc.directory's **W3C** document into `PlcDidDocument` — whose `rotation_keys` is `#[serde(default)]` and documented as "Empty if only populated from the W3C DID Document". The claim flow then persists a PLC-shaped doc with `rotationKeys: []` → badge "Unknown" → migrate entry hidden, even though plc.directory shows the device key at `rotationKeys[0]`.

## Fix (extends PR #202)

1. `claim::submit_claim` re-fetches `GET {plc}/{did}/data` (the PLC data document) and caches that, like the MM-300 fix did for migrate/recovery. Shared `PdsClient::fetch_plc_data_document` helper used by all three.
2. **Self-heal**: existing installs already have poisoned caches (the phone's claimed identity, the sim throwaway). New `refresh_did_doc` IPC command (fetch `/data` + re-store); `IdentityListHome.loadData` invokes it best-effort whenever the cached doc is missing or has no `rotationKeys`, so stale caches repair on the next home load with no user action.

Wallet-only; ships in the same build as MM-300.

Base directory for this skill: /Users/jacob.zweifel/.claude/skills/pr-review-comments

# Batch PR Review-Comment Triage

Pull every unresolved review thread on the current PR in one command, then triage the batch. The user should never have to paste review comments one at a time.

## Fetch unresolved threads

Determine the PR number for the current branch (`gh pr view --json number -q .number`), then:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='
query($owner:String!,$repo:String!,$pr:Int!){
  repository(owner:$owner,name:$repo){
    pullRequest(number:$pr){
      reviewThreads(first:100){
        nodes{
          isResolved isOutdated path line
          comments(first:30){nodes{author{login} body url}}
        }
      }
    }
  }
}' -F owner=<owner> -F repo=<repo> -F pr=<number> \
| jq '[.data.repository.pullRequest.reviewThreads.nodes[]
       | select(.isResolved==false)
       | {path, line, isOutdated,
          comments: [.comments.nodes[] | {author: .author.login, url, body}]}]'
```

Also fetch top-level (non-thread) review bodies and issue comments if the bot posts summaries there:

```bash
gh pr view <number> --json reviews,comments
```

## Triage the batch

For each unresolved thread, classify before fixing anything:

1. **Correctness / security / portability** — verify the claim against the actual code, then fix if real. Automated reviewers assert confidently and are sometimes wrong; refute with evidence when they are.
2. **Legitimate but out of scope** — file a follow-up issue rather than growing the PR.
3. **Pure style nit / preference** — decline with a one-line reason.

Present the full disposition table (thread → classification → action) to the user in ONE message before applying fixes, so they approve the batch rather than each item. Note that every fix-commit re-triggers CI and (for assertive bots like CodeRabbit) a fresh review round that tends to find one more micro-nit — batch fixes into a single commit where possible.

## Resolving threads

After pushing fixes, reply/resolve via:

```bash
gh api graphql -f query='mutation($id:ID!){resolveReviewThread(input:{threadId:$id}){thread{isResolved}}}' -F id=<threadId>
```

(Include `id` in the reviewThreads query above if you plan to resolve threads programmatically.)

1. **Typed error (Major)** — accepted and fixed: `refresh_did_doc` now returns `RefreshDidDocError` with `FETCH_FAILED`/`STORAGE_FAILED` codes, matching the `{ code: SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE }` contract every other IPC command honors, instead of an opaque `String`.

3. **Dedupe the HTTP fetch pattern (Trivial, self-rated low-value)** — declined with reasoning posted: pre-existing pattern, the three functions have genuinely different response handling, and this PR stays a targeted fix on the MM-241 critical path.

hm, merged and got the latest testflight on my device. when I sign in to my current pds, the bsky pds screen shows with an authorize screen requesting an oauth token as far as I can see. Shouldn't I be getting a login screen requesting that I input my username and password?

Yes — that's exactly right, and it's the deliberate design difference between the two flows:

- **The claim flow (leg a)** used a username/password login screen inside the app, because its next steps were PLC identity operations (`requestPlcOperationSignature`/`signPlcOperation`) that bsky.social only permits with a full session — no OAuth token a third-party app can obtain grants those (that was the whole MM-289 saga, ADR-0021).
- **The outbound migration flow (leg b)** doesn't need any identity operation from bsky — the PLC op is **self-signed by your phone's Secure Enclave key**, which is the entire point of what you're about to prove. All it needs from bsky as source is repo export, blob fetch, preferences, service auth, and the final deactivate — all covered by a standard OAuth grant (`transition:generic`). So the source login is the in-app OAuth sheet (ASWebAuthenticationSession), not a password form.

As for why you jumped straight to the *authorize* page without typing credentials: the OAuth sheet shares Safari's cookie jar, so if you've signed into bsky.social in Safari before (including during earlier testing), bsky recognizes the session and skips its login form, going directly to consent. If you'd never logged in there, you'd see bsky's own username/password page first, then this same consent screen.

content.text:
Full picture, cleanly reproduced and probes revoked:

| Credential tier | `getServiceAuth` for `createAccount` |
|---|---|
| Full session (password `createSession`) | ✅ mints |
| **Privileged** app password | ✅ mints |
| Plain app password / **OAuth `transition:generic`** ← your phone | ❌ `insufficient access` |

So bsky gates minting a `createAccount` service token at the **privileged** tier, and the wallet's outbound source login sits below it. This is MM-289's sibling: the orchestrator's design assumed `transition:generic` covers everything a *self-signed* migration needs from the source — true for repo/blobs/preferences/deactivate, false for this one mint. Leg (r) couldn't catch it because Custos's `require_rpc` is laxer than the reference and lets `transition:generic` mint any method (an MM-292-family divergence that masked the wall).

Filing the ticket with this evidence. On the fix, two real options:

1. **Password source login for outbound migration** (my recommendation): swap `prepare_source_auth`/`complete_source_auth` OAuth for the claim flow's password `createSession` machinery (`authenticate_source_pds` already exists, with 2FA handling and the HTTPS/account-match guards). Consistent with ADR-0021's logic — migrating away is exactly the class of account-authority operation the reference gates behind a real session. Honest UX: "sign in with your password to move your account." Works identically against bsky and Custos sources, so legs (b)/(c)/(d) all use one path.
2. **Request `transition:chat.bsky` in the OAuth scope** to reach the privileged tier — technically works, but semantically absurd (asking for DM access to migrate) and fragile against future reference changes. I'd reject it.

Option 1 touches the migration flow's auth step end to end (backend command swap + the source-auth screen becomes a password screen, mirroring `PdsAuthScreen`), plus an ADR-0021 amendment noting migration joins the claim flow on the password path — and then a new TestFlight build. Want me to build it now, or is this one you want to take like MM-289?
go ahead and build it

input.title: Outbound migration source login must be a full session — bsky refuses getServiceAuth(createAccount) for transition:generic
input.description:
## Found by

MM-241 leg (b), on device: the orchestrator failed at create-destination-account with `SERVICE_AUTH_FAILED` ("Couldn't authorize with the destination PDS").

## Evidence (curl-reproduced against bsky.social)

`getServiceAuth?aud=did:web:ezpds-staging.up.railway.app&lxm=com.atproto.server.createAccount`:

| Credential tier | Result |
|---|---|
| Full session (password createSession) | ✅ mints token |
| Privileged app password | ✅ mints token |
| Plain app password / OAuth `transition:generic` (what the wallet holds) | ❌ `InvalidRequest: insufficient access to request a service auth token for the following method: com.atproto.server.createAccount` |

The reference PDS gates service-token minting for privileged methods at the privileged tier. The orchestrator's design assumption — `transition:generic` suffices for a *self-signed* migration's source calls — holds for repo/blobs/preferences/deactivate but not this mint. MM-289's sibling.

Leg (r) masked it: Custos's `require_rpc` lets `transition:generic` mint any lxm (an MM-292-family laxness — noted there).

## Fix

Switch the outbound-migration **source login** from the OAuth PKCE pair (`prepare_source_auth`/`complete_source_auth`) to the claim flow's password `createSession` machinery (ADR-0021 pattern): full-session Bearer client, HTTPS guard, account-match guard, email-2FA support. One consistent path for bsky and Custos sources (legs b/c/d). MigrationSourceAuthScreen becomes a password form mirroring PdsAuthScreen. Amend ADR-0021: migration source login joins the claim flow on the password path — a full session is required to mint the `createAccount` service token, per reference enforcement.

Rejected alternative: requesting `transition:chat.bsky` to reach the privileged OAuth tier — semantically wrong (DM access to migrate) and fragile.
